risk_review.notes: Independently checked Statement and all four proof steps against the complete current finite Reynolds proof and finite-ensemble Definition. F1 applies to periodic lifts on the open domain R^d with zero continuous forcing, fixed normalized nonnegative weights and common nu>=0; F2 gives zero weighted fluctuation and gradient; F3 gives the exact total-energy split. On each compact time subinterval times the periodic cell, continuous time derivatives justify differentiation under the integral; continuous second spatial derivatives justify integration by parts. Periodic endpoint values cancel all coordinate divergence integrals, including pressure and convection. Rowwise divergence gives -integral(bar u dot div R)=+integral R:grad(bar u). Memberwise viscous terms are nonpositive; the gradient cross terms vanish by F2, giving the opposite transfer sign in step 3.1. The resulting continuous derivatives justify both endpoint identities by the fundamental theorem of calculus and exact transfer cancellation. No sign claim for transfer, solution existence, physical applicability or empirical certainty is inferred. N=1, zero weights, nu=0, singular/zero R and constant opposite members all satisfy the identities; empty ensembles are excluded, endpoints lie inside I, and no choice or iff argument occurs.
